cause_quote: #191711 enabled statement timing for hydration reads (`operationLabel === "session.lifecycle.delete" || hydration ? startSqliteStatementTiming(hydration)`), but the timing only counts statements on connections wrapped by `observeConnection`, which the ordinary read-only agent opener never called.
user_saw: Slow cron transcript hydration warnings in the Gateway log reported zero SQL statements even though SQLite did substantial reads.
summary: Wraps the ordinary read-only agent database connection with the existing statement observer before statement caching, and bounds workspace sweep batch selection instead of copying the whole pending set.
reasoning: The reported defect is the hydration slow-hold warning showing statementTiming.count 0; per-statement attribution for hydration was first enabled by 9eb72a0fbc17 (#191711) three hours earlier, whose own benchmark wrapped its handle explicitly and so missed that openOpenClawAgentDatabaseReadOnly never called observeConnection. I read #191711's sqlite-transaction.ts and observation.ts diffs; I did not confirm whether any earlier attribution path also used the read-only opener, hence medium. The sweep allocation change is a pure performance improvement and not part of the defect.
